summary: Imperial Steam is a tight economic pick-up-and-deliver game where you hire workers, lay track, staff factories, and fulfill contracts before the connection to Trieste triggers sudden-death scoring. It's a spiritual successor to the Age of Steam/Indonesia lineage, rewarding efficient engine-building and route timing over direct confrontation.
praised: meaningful decisions on nearly every action
strong sense of progression as the map fills up
criticised: notable downtime at higher player counts
punishing for players who mismanage cash flow early

interaction.kind: competition for shared routes, contracts, and market space
interaction.detail: Players build on the same map and compete for the same limited contracts, workers, and delivery routes, indirectly blocking each other by claiming space and depressing shared markets rather than attacking directly. Each player still runs their own factory/track engine, so much of the state is personal even though the map and contract pool are shared.

scoring.why: Final score combines contract-fulfillment points, factory and network value, company share ownership, and leftover cash converted at game end, so no single track dominates the outcome.
scoring.how_you_win: You build track and factories to deliver goods and fulfill profitable contracts while buying shares in companies; once someone completes the Trieste connection, everyone totals contracts, shares, and cash into a final net-worth score, and the highest total wins.
